what: The rule that tags a held policy action (policy_actions) as touching large loads, interconnection, transmission cost or tax credits. Code applies it (warehouse/derived/policy_action_tags.py); no model reads a row. Method: docs/methods/policy_action_tags.md.
how_text_is_read: The title, the abstract and (since version 3) the first paragraph of the action's printed text in the Federal Register, each on its own: lower case; every hyphen and dash becomes a space; white space collapsed. The phrases under 'strip' are taken out first (a company's name is not a topic). A term matches when its words stand in the text as whole words, in order. A field the row does not hold is empty.

municipal.rule: An action whose title or abstract holds one of these phrases is about municipal permitting, zoning or a local hearing: it is out of scope and never tagged, whatever else it says.

large_load.what: The action names large electricity customers or the connecting of them.

interconnection.what: The action is about connecting generation or load to the power grid. The interconnection of gas pipelines, of liquefied natural gas plant or of telecommunications is not the power grid's.

transmission_cost.what: The action is about what electric transmission costs or who pays for it: rates, formula rates, cost allocation, charges. A transmission line's siting or environmental review is not a cost action, and neither is a gas pipeline company with 'Transmission' in its name.

tax_credit.what: The action is about a federal or state energy tax credit. A bill credit (California's climate credit), a credit rating, an emissions credit or allowance, a renewable energy certificate and an engineering 'credit' taken in a safety analysis are not tax credits.

changes.what: The rule as first written, before any row was read (run of 8 October 2026: 7 actions tagged).

The one correction after reading the 7 tagged and 40 untagged actions of seed 154. (a) transmission_cost: 'formula rate' and 'formula rates' now need 'transmission service', 'transmission formula' or 'transmission rate' beside them, not the bare word 'transmission': version 1 tagged the two notices of Rate Order No. WAPA-222, the rates of a balancing authority's ancillary services (scheduling, reserves, imbalance), which are not what transmission costs. (b) transmission_cost: the word 'transmission' with 'electricity customers', 'ratepayer', 'ratepayers', 'customer bills' or 'who pays' in the title or abstract now tags: version 1 missed the California commission's release on its transmission advocacy for electricity customers at FERC, whose title holds no cost word. (c) Dockets listed by number: version 1 could not tag the notices in FERC dockets EL26-67 to EL26-72, whose titles hold only the names of an operator and its transmission owners; a notice whose docket field holds a listed docket now takes that docket's tags.

Session 157. The terms, the exclusions and the listed dockets are those of version 2, unchanged. The one change: the rule now also reads 'first_paragraph', the first paragraph of the action's printed text in the Federal Register (policy_sources.py reads each document's printed text once), because a FERC notice has no abstract in the Register's record and its title is often only the parties' names. The municipal phrases, each tag's exclusions and 'needs_any' are read across the three fields. The site applies this same file to the rows it reads (site/data/policy/tag_rules.json is a byte-for-byte copy).

dockets.rule: A notice whose title holds only the parties' names and that has no abstract cannot match a term. Where its docket field holds one of these docket numbers (a whole number: EL26-67 stands in 'Docket No. EL26-67-000'), it takes that docket's tags; the matched field is 'docket' and the matched term the docket number. Each docket is listed with the regulator's own order that says what the proceeding is, read in session 154 (large_load_rules holds its sentence). The municipal rule, the agencies in scope and each tag's exclusions hold for these rows too. A notice whose docket field lists more than three docket numbers is a combined notice (a notice of staff attendance at a meeting lists every docket that may be spoken of): it takes no docket's tags. 'grids' names the grid operator each docket is about, by the order's own caption.
